input.text: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.

requirement.raw: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.

ambiguities.question: What load must the system handle (new links/month, redirects/sec at peak)?
ambiguities.default: 10M new links/month, 100:1 read:write, peak = 10x average (~4k redirects/s); stateless horizontally-scalable service tier

assumptions.text: 'scalable' interpreted as: 10M new links/month, 100:1 read:write, peak = 10x average (~4k redirects/s); stateless horizontally-scalable service tier

llm_suggested_questions: What traffic volume, data size, latency targets, and availability guarantees must the service support?
Which API operations and access controls are required, including custom aliases, link expiration, updates, deletion, and authentication?
What persistence and analytics requirements apply, including consistency, backup and recovery, tracked metrics, reporting freshness, data retention, and privacy constraints?
requirement.title: Scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence and analytics
requirement.problem_statement: Build a horizontally-scalable, read-heavy (~100:1) HTTP service that creates short codes for long URLs, redirects with minimal latency, persists links durably, and records click analytics off the hot path, with contract-first APIs, validation against abuse, and a test-verified implementation.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1 Given a valid https URL, POST /api/v1/links returns 201 with a 7-char code and short_url.
AC-2 Given an existing code, GET /{code} returns 302 with Location equal to the original URL.
AC-3 Given an unknown or deleted code, GET /{code} returns 404 with a JSON error body.
AC-4 Given a custom alias that is taken, POST returns 409; if invalid, 400.
AC-5 Given non-http(s), private-host or credential-bearing URLs, POST returns 400.
AC-6 After redirects occur and the recorder flushes, GET /api/v1/links/{code}/stats reports total clicks, unique visitors, daily series, referrers and devices.
AC-7 Links persist across process restarts (same database file).
AC-8 More than the configured requests/minute from one client on POST returns 429.
AC-9 openapi.json exactly matches the implemented routes (contract test).

capabilities.name: Create short link
capabilities.detail: POST url (+ optional custom alias) -> unique short code

capabilities.name: Redirect
capabilities.detail: GET /{code} -> HTTP redirect to the original URL, low latency

capabilities.name: Link management
capabilities.detail: fetch metadata and delete a link

capabilities.name: Persistence
capabilities.detail: links survive restarts; versioned schema migrations

capabilities.name: Click analytics
capabilities.detail: total / unique clicks, daily series, referrers, devices

capabilities.name: Abuse protection
capabilities.detail: URL validation, rate limiting, optional API-key auth

lead_plan.rationale: Establish the architecture first, then design the API contract and persistence schema in parallel. Implementation proceeds alongside risk-driven verification planning; independent tests and documentation feed a final quality gate and evidence summary.

design.style: stateless HTTP service + repository port + async analytics pipeline

components.name: HTTP/WSGI layer (app.py)
components.responsibility: routing, request parsing, error mapping, auth, rate limit, request-id

components.name: ShortenerService (service.py)
components.responsibility: business rules: validate, allocate code (retry), cache, resolve, stats

components.name: Validation (validation.py)
components.responsibility: URL/alias policy: scheme allow-list, private-host block, length

components.name: Repository (storage.py)
components.responsibility: persistence port; SQLite adapter; versioned migrations; batch click insert

components.name: TTLCache (cache.py)
components.responsibility: bounded LRU+TTL read-through cache for redirects

components.name: ClickRecorder (analytics.py)
components.responsibility: bounded queue, background batch flush, device classification, visitor hashing

data_flows: create: client -> app (auth, rate limit) -> service.validate -> repo.create_link (UNIQUE) -> 201
redirect: client -> app -> service.resolve -> cache hit? else repo.get_link -> recorder.record (non-blocking) -> 302
analytics: recorder queue -> batch flush -> click_events (+ click_daily upsert) -> GET /stats aggregates
scale_out: run N identical stateless nodes behind an L4/L7 load balancer
swap SQLite adapter for PostgreSQL (hash-shard on code) or DynamoDB
replace in-process cache with Redis; add CDN for 301/hot links
replace recorder with Kafka producer + ClickHouse consumer

adrs.title: Short-code generation: random base62 with unique-constraint retry
adrs.decision: random base62, 7 chars, retry on unique violation
adrs.why: No cross-node coordination, codes are non-enumerable, per-insert collision probability is n/62^7 (~0.03% at 1B links) so a bounded retry loop is enough.
adrs.tradeoffs: Needs a unique index and a retry path; counters are collision-free but leak volume and are enumerable; hash truncation makes dedup easy but collides on truncation and leaks URL equality.

adrs.title: Persistence behind a Repository port; SQLite for the prototype
adrs.decision: Repository interface + SQLite(WAL) now; PostgreSQL (hash-sharded by code) or DynamoDB in production
adrs.why: Access pattern is pure key-value (code -> url) with ~100:1 reads; the port isolates storage choice from business logic so scale-out is an adapter swap, not a rewrite.
adrs.tradeoffs: SQLite is single-writer and single-node: fine for a runnable, zero-dependency prototype, not for the stated scale.

adrs.title: Redirect uses HTTP 302 (configurable to 301)
adrs.why: Browsers cache 301s, so repeat clicks bypass us and analytics under-count; 302 keeps every click observable and allows later edits/expiry.
adrs.tradeoffs: Higher redirect traffic and no browser/CDN caching offload; 301 is cheaper if analytics are not needed.

adrs.title: Analytics are off the redirect hot path (buffered, batched, lossy under overload)
adrs.decision: bounded queue + background batch flusher; Kafka/ClickHouse is the production path
adrs.why: Redirect latency must not depend on write throughput of the analytics store. Batching turns N inserts into 1 transaction.
adrs.tradeoffs: Clicks can be lost on crash (<= flush interval) or dropped when the queue is full (counted in a metric). Stats are eventually consistent.

adrs.title: Read-through TTL/LRU cache for redirect lookups
adrs.why: Traffic is Zipfian; a small cache absorbs the hot set and cuts DB reads dramatically.
adrs.tradeoffs: Deleted links can still redirect for up to TTL on other nodes; the local node invalidates immediately.

adrs.title: Privacy-preserving analytics
adrs.decision: salted SHA-256 visitor hash; raw IP never stored
adrs.why: Unique-visitor counts without retaining personal data (GDPR data minimisation).
adrs.tradeoffs: Hash of IP+UA is an approximation (NAT, UA changes); cannot be reversed for debugging.

adrs.title: Stateless service tier; per-node rate limiting
options: stateless nodes behind a load balancer
adrs.decision: stateless; token-bucket rate limit per client per node
adrs.why: Any node can serve any request, so scaling is adding nodes.
adrs.tradeoffs: Per-node limits are approximate (effective limit = limit x nodes); a Redis-backed limiter makes it exact.

adrs.title: Contract-first API (OpenAPI 3) enforced by tests
adrs.decision: openapi.json is generated first and a contract test fails if routes drift
adrs.why: Parallel agents (code, tests, docs) coordinate through one contract instead of guessing each other's output.
adrs.tradeoffs: Spec and code must be kept in sync; the contract test is what makes that cheap.

domain.mitigation: UNIQUE constraint + bounded retry; code length configurable
scheme allow-list (http/https), no credentials in URL, block loopback/private/link-local hosts, length cap; prod: Safe Browsing check + abuse reporting
bounded queue, drop counter, flush on shutdown; documented eventual consistency

domain.risk: Hot-key / viral link overloads the datastore
domain.mitigation: TTL+LRU cache in front of the DB; CDN/Redis tier in production
token-bucket rate limit per client, optional API keys, non-sequential codes
local invalidation on delete; bounded TTL (60s) for other nodes

domain.risk: Datastore is a single point of failure
domain.mitigation: Repository port; production: managed replicated store; /healthz checks DB
salted visitor hash; no raw IP persisted
versioned, forward-only, additive migrations applied transactionally on start

domain.risk: Generated code deviates from the contract (agentic failure mode)
domain.mitigation: contract conformance + schema parity + executed tests are mandatory validation gates

agentic.mitigation: requirement is treated as data; injection patterns are flagged and ignored; agents cannot execute free-text instructions

agentic.risk: Agent writes outside its remit / path traversal
agentic.mitigation: Workspace sandbox + per-task write scopes + extension allow-list
bounded attempts (3) and bounded repair rounds (2); then fail and escalate to a human
validator gate; downstream tasks of a failed task are SKIPPED, never run on bad inputs
two human approval gates; release dir written only after approval; original repo never mutated

layers.scope: service + Repository on in-memory SQLite, fake clock
WSGI in-process API tests + real TCP server + restart persistence

layers.tool: generated contract test + static AST check

layers.scope: load smoke (p50/p95/p99, rps) against a live node

steps: static checks: syntax (AST), secret scan, size/extension policy
run full test-suite in an isolated subprocess (timeout, scrubbed env)

tasks.description: Define the test strategy and verification steps, derived from the risks, before any test is written.

tasks.description: MODEL-BACKED agent: writes the service (greenfield) or proposes anchored edits to existing code (llm_change).

tasks.title: Write independent specification and acceptance tests
tasks.description: MODEL-BACKED agent: writes tests from the specification only, never seeing the code (independent oracle).

tasks.title: Document operation, architecture, and mitigations
tasks.description: Write the documentation: README, architecture, ADRs, risks (new system); change record and changelog (change); proposal (analysis).

tasks.title: Run quality gates and acceptance checks
tasks.description: The quality gate: runs static, contract, schema, test, regression and traceability checks. Blames producers by role.
